243: Four authors have written the book that they themselves have always lacked. BØSSEDANMARK is a strong collection of short stories that describes the lives of 20 different gays, in 20 different places in Denmark. The book will be published on 16 August 2021 during Copenhagen Pride. In connection with the publication, there is a talk with the authors in Arnold Busck in Købmagergade on 15 August at 14-16. There is also an open publication reception on 16 August in Bøssehuset in Christiania.
244: There are gays everywhere in Denmark. Each little patch has a few. Each block of flats. Each parish. From Copenhagen to Vester Skerninge. From Allinge to Hvide Sande.
245: In the short story collection BØSSEDANMARK we meet both the politician, the high school student and the aid client. They are boundary-pushing, humorous and extroverted. They are introverted, sensitive or live in hiding. We follow them when they practice kidnapping sex in Aalborg and when they try to be self-sufficient in Lolland, when they live dramatic double lives or accidentally end up in a gay association in Herning, in search of love.
246: The short stories describe common human experiences such as loneliness, falling in love, desire, dreams and difficult relationships. The book can thus be read by everyone, regardless of sexual preferences.
247: I wrote the short story collection BØSSEDANMARK together with Nikolaj Tange Lange, Mads Ananda Lodahl and Tomas Lagermand Lundme. I drew inspiration from places and human encounters that have been important to me: friendships, sexual relationships, colleagues, lovers and both the family I was born into and the one I chose myself.

250: "The collection of short stories focuses on what gay life can look like today," say the four authors. "Being gay in Denmark today is a different experience than it was 10, 20 or 40 years ago. But also writing about gay life experiences is something different today than a few years ago. Gay life can be unfolded in a more complex, diverse and nuanced way than ever before, where it was previously associated with guilt and shame.
251: For some of us this is a book with sex as the focal point, but for others of us it is other and underlying aspects that are most important. It is our hope that readers from all over the country will be able to see themselves reflected in the stories, and that the book will be able to contribute to a sense of community across all of society's many divides."

1162: When I grew up in the Faroe Islands, no one talked about gays, lips or trans people. I felt a bit like a refugee when I came to Denmark in 1990. But today the Faroe Islands are going through a big development in the LGBT area (Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transsexual). However, I have not seen or heard of any Faroese trances yet. But they are also found everywhere.
1163: Inspired by all this, I have made a 15 min. Faroese Trash Drag Art Film. Through humor and surrealism, it can be easier to talk about difficult subjects and reach a new reality. That your neighbor is actually a man who wears women's clothes.
1164: The film is called "Snoribolla Genturnar" (Bussemand's Girls) The name comes from my teenage urge to say dangerous words like Gay, Dick, Asshole. But in public I didn't dare say anything ruder than Busseman. That has since changed.
1165: In addition to myself, who of course speaks Faroese, the married couple Nikolai & René Noesgaard Myntman, who neither speak nor understand Faroese, are participating. Everything they say in the film are sentences I have written down on paper with audio script which they then say out loud when the camera is filming. The film is available with Danish and English subtitles. But you don't have to understand what is being said at all. It's more the way it's said that works.
